knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The inspection is done against the signed checklist, line by line, so that the record can be checked later. Impressions and opinions are not a record.
Pre-existing damage is recorded as found and classified against the pre-work record. It is not recorded as cleaning failure, and the cleaner does not pay a deduction.
The handover describes the clean and the evidence. Bond release is decided by the parties or by an order, so the cleaner does not guarantee it.

practicalCriteria: In a simulated inspection, the worker checks each line of the signed checklist in order, marks any line that cannot be checked as inaccessible, and records the result for every line.

Given a simulated cracked tile and a simulated overlooked shelf, the worker classifies the tile as pre-existing damage using the pre-work record, corrects and reinspects the shelf as missed cleaning, and records both.
Given a simulated request to confirm a bond return, the worker declines the guarantee and gives the handover pack and follow-up contact instead.
The worker takes a simulated photograph with no people or private documents in frame, and retakes any photograph that shows them.
passRule: Every checklist line recorded. Each finding classified against the pre-work record, with missed cleaning corrected and reinspected. Bond guarantee declined. Photographs free of people and private documents. Observed in a supervised simulation, with assessor sign-off. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Authorised photographs with timestamps, and any retake record
stopWorkCriteria: Inspection carried out by impression rather than against the signed checklist
Pre-existing or permanent damage recorded as a cleaning failure without evidence
Bond or deposit outcome guaranteed in writing or in conversation
Photograph shared that shows people or private documents
